metadata.note:
The Chicago Great Western - the Corn Belt Route, and on its Chicago - Twin Cities main the Maple Leaf Route - was A. B. Stickney's granger railroad, an X of secondary main lines crossing at Oelwein, Iowa, and reaching Chicago, the Twin Cities, Omaha and Kansas City with about 1,400 route miles. It grew out of the Minnesota & Northwestern, which opened St. Paul to the Iowa line on 2 October 1885, absorbed the Dubuque & North Western in 1886, was extended from Hayfield, Minnesota into Illinois in 1887, and reached Forest Park - and, over the Baltimore & Ohio Chicago Terminal, Chicago's Grand Central Station - on 9 February 1888. As the Chicago, St. Paul & Kansas City it pushed south from Des Moines to St. Joseph in 1890 and Kansas City in 1891, taking the Chicago Great Western name in 1892. The last arm was the Omaha line: the Mason City & Fort Dodge was taken over in March 1901, the Manly Junction - Mason City link built in 1901-02 and the 132.87 mi Fort Dodge - Council Bluffs extension opened on 1 January 1904.

The CGW was always the longest way between any two of its cities, and its passenger business died unusually early. The overnight Chicago - St. Paul train, the Legionnaire of 1925 and the Minnesotan from 1930, lost its name on 10 May 1949 and ran for the last time on 11 August 1956 - after which the railroad had no passenger trains east of Oelwein at all. The Oelwein - Clarion arm of the Omaha line had already gone: train 35's last run was on 26 June 1950. That left exactly two through trains, and they went in turn - the Mill Cities Limited, Twin Cities to Kansas City, on 27 April 1962, and the Twin Cities - Omaha Nebraska Limited / Twin City Limited on 29-30 September 1965. For its last two and a half years the Chicago Great Western carried freight and nothing else, until the Chicago & North Western absorbed it on 1 July 1968. Nothing here is therefore drawn past 1965, and most of the system stops well before that; the 1968 merger and the 1971 Amtrak date are both irrelevant to this map.

Four features cover the system. They deliberately overlap: the Minneapolis - Hayfield stretch is drawn three times and Hayfield - Oelwein twice, because those corridors kept passenger trains after the Chicago trains stopped, and each feature's drawn years are the years its own service ran.

https://www.american-rails.com/cgw.html — route structure, the roster of named trains, 'by 1956 only two through trains remained', the 27 April 1962 Mill Cities last run and the 29 September 1965 final departure from Omaha's Burlington Station.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Trains/ICC_valuations/Mason_City_and_Fort_Dodge_Railroad — ICC valuation of the Mason City & Fort Dodge: Hayfield to Council Bluffs and Clarion to Oelwein, with segment mileages and dates (Mason City-Fort Dodge 72.60 mi 1886, Manly Junction-Mason City 9.20 mi 1901, Clarion-Hampton 26.83 mi 1902, Fort Dodge-Council Bluffs 132.87 mi 1903, Oelwein-Waverly 29.25 mi 1904, 89.38 mi purchased 1905).

https://www.openstreetmap.org/ — all geometry, via Overpass: ways tagged old_railway_operator=CGW plus the Great Western, Heritage, Aiken, Wapsi Great Western, Shooting Star, Cerro Gordo County, Rolling Prairie, Waverly and Chichaqua Valley rail trails built on the right of way.
not_yet_sourced: The Rochester, Minnesota services are not drawn at all. The Minnesotan split a Rochester section at McIntire, Iowa, and the CGW ran the Blue Bird, Red Bird and Rochester Special between the Twin Cities and Rochester over the leased Wisconsin, Minnesota & Pacific, but no start or discontinuance dates for any of them were found, so rather than guess the years nothing is drawn. The McIntire - Rochester grade is in OSM as a 23 mi razed way named 'Chicago Great Western' and would be easy to trace once dates exist.

Likewise undrawn for want of dates: the Randolph - Mankato and Red Wing - Rochester - Winona lines of the Wisconsin, Minnesota & Pacific, the Sycamore - De Kalb, Sumner - Waverly, Cedar Falls Junction - Cedar Falls and Eden - Mantorville branches, and the Fort Dodge - Lehigh branch.
Whether any of those branches carried passengers late enough to matter, and when their passenger service ended, is unchecked.
Every headway_min here is an estimate; no CGW public timetable was consulted for any segment. Only the Chicago-Minneapolis average speed is derived from a documented running time.
The exact year through passenger service began on the Oelwein - Clarion arm (drawn from 1905, the year the Waverly - Hampton link was purchased) is not established.
The 1891 start for Twin Cities - Kansas City service is the year the route was completed to Kansas City, not a documented first passenger timetable; likewise 1904 for Twin Cities - Omaha.
Source conflict recorded, not resolved: american-rails gives 27 April 1962 for the Mill Cities Limited's last run, while a Classic Trains caption dates train 5 at St. Joseph to 28 April 1962.
The 26 June 1950 end of the Oelwein - Clarion service rests on a single caption reached through search; the underlying page could not be fetched.

properties.line: Chicago Great Western: Minnesotan (Chicago – Twin Cities)
properties.speed_source: 435 mi in about 12 h 25 min (Wikipedia, 'Minnesotan') = 35 mph = 56 km/h. That is an end-to-end average including stops, not a track speed.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 441 mi Chicago Grand Central - Dubuque - Oelwein - Hayfield - St. Paul - Minneapolis against the 435 mi documented for Chicago-Minneapolis (Wikipedia, 'Minnesotan'), 1.3% long. About 345 mi is real OSM geometry: the abandoned B&OCT approach to Grand Central and the CSX Altenheim Subdivision (the B&OCT line the CGW used under trackage rights) out to Forest Park; the Great Western Trail and the CGW abandoned grade Villa Park - St. Charles - Wasco - Sycamore; the abandoned CGW grade Byron - south of Freeport; the Aiken Trail; the CB&Q (now BNSF) river line Galena Junction - East Dubuque that the CGW used under trackage rights; the Heritage Trail and the abandoned grade Dubuque - Dyersville - Oelwein; the abandoned grade Oelwein - Sumner - New Hampton - Riceville - McIntire; the Wapsi Great Western Line and the CGW grade McIntire - Taopi - Elkton - Renova - Sargeant - Hayfield; and the abandoned 'Chicago Great Western Railway' grade Dodge Center - Kenyon - Randolph - Rosemount plus live track into South St. Paul, St. Paul Union Depot and Minneapolis. Straight-line substitutions where OSM has nothing of the grade: Sycamore-Byron 30 mi, Freeport-Pearl City 12 mi, Pearl City-Stockton 11 mi, Stockton-Elizabeth 11 mi, Elizabeth-Aiken 10 mi, St. Charles-Wasco 5 mi, Little Cedar-Taopi 5 mi. Shorter straight bridges over gaps in the mapping total about 12 mi (largest: Mantorville Junction-Dodge Center 2.7, Taopi-Adams Junction 2.0, Forest Park-Villa Park 1.6, Villa Park-Wheaton 1.5, McIntire 1.7, Oelwein-Sumner 1.3). Total approximated: about 96 mi of 441. No era mismatch is known - the alignment did not move over the drawn years, and the Winston Tunnel east of Galena (bored 1888, the longest in Illinois) falls inside the straight-line Stockton-Elizabeth-Aiken stretch, so the drawn line does not follow it.

segments.note: Through Chicago - Twin Cities service. The Minnesota & Northwestern opened St. Paul to the Iowa state line on 2 October 1885 and absorbed the Dubuque & North Western in 1886; the Hayfield - Illinois unit was finished in 1887 and the Chicago, St. Paul & Kansas City completed the Illinois line into Forest Park, opening it for service on 9 February 1888. From Forest Park CGW trains ran into Grand Central Station over the Baltimore & Ohio Chicago Terminal. The company took the Chicago Great Western name in 1892; the flagship of these years was the Great Western Limited. The headway is an estimate standing for roughly two through trains a day each way - it is not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the 1885/1887/1888 construction dates and the Forest Park - Grand Central trackage-rights arrangement come from the sources below; the headway is an unsourced estimate.

segments.note: The overnight Chicago - St. Paul train, launched as the Legionnaire on 16 January 1925 and given its permanent name, the Minnesotan, in 1930. 435 mi Chicago to Minneapolis in about 12 h 25 min behind a 4-6-2 Pacific, with a section that split at McIntire, Iowa to serve Rochester, Minnesota (359 mi from Chicago). It could not match the Milwaukee Road's or the North Western's more direct routes. The named train ran for the last time on 10 May 1949. One train a day each way, hence 1440 min.
sources: Segment-level: the 16 January 1925 launch, the 1930 renaming, the 12 h 25 min schedule, the McIntire Rochester split and the 10 May 1949 end are all from the Wikipedia article on the Minnesotan.

segments.note: After the name was dropped the Chicago - St. Paul run carried on as unnamed trains 7 and 8, reduced to a single EMD F-unit or a doodlebug hauling an RPO, a baggage car and a coach. The last run was on 11 August 1956, ending all CGW passenger service east of Oelwein; by then chicagorailfan lists trains 7/8 simply as Chicago - Dubuque - Oelwein. The Twin Cities end of this corridor kept passenger trains after 1956 - see the Mill Cities Limited and Nebraska Limited features, which is why this feature stops in 1956 and they do not. Freight lasted longer: the Chicago & North Western, which absorbed the CGW on 1 July 1968, abandoned the Illinois line piecemeal, St. Charles - Sycamore in 1977 and Sycamore - Byron in 1981.
sources: Segment-level: the 11 August 1956 last run is from the Wikipedia article on the Minnesotan; the reduced consist and the 1956 date are corroborated by chicagorailfan's CGW train list, the abandonment dates by frrandp.

properties.line: Chicago Great Western: Mill Cities Limited (Twin Cities – Kansas City)
properties.speed_source: Estimate only: no CGW timetable was consulted. 558 mi overnight in roughly 16 h would be about 35 mph = 55 km/h, in line with the measured 35 mph of the Chicago-Minneapolis run.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 558 mi Minneapolis - St. Paul - Hayfield - Oelwein - Waterloo - Marshalltown - Des Moines - St. Joseph - Leavenworth - Kansas City. There is no single published figure for the CGW Twin Cities - Kansas City distance to check against; the derived comparison is about 552 mi (Oelwein - Minneapolis about 186 mi, from 435 mi Chicago-Minneapolis less about 249 mi Chicago-Oelwein, plus about 366 mi Oelwein - Kansas City), so the trace runs about 1% long. Minneapolis - Oelwein is the same geometry as the Minnesotan feature and carries the same caveats (about 12 mi approximated, the largest single piece the 5 mi Little Cedar - Taopi straight line). South of Oelwein the trace is almost entirely real: the CGW abandoned grade and surviving track Oelwein - Fairbank - Dunkerton - Waterloo, the abandoned grade Hudson - Reinbeck - Marshalltown, the Chichaqua Valley Trail Baxter - Mingo - Bondurant, the Great Western Trail Des Moines - Martensdale and the 34 mi abandoned CGW grade Martensdale - Lorimor - Talmage, then CGW-tagged grade and surviving line through Diagonal, Blockton, Sheridan, Ravenwood, Conception Junction, Guilford, Savannah, St. Joseph, Dearborn, Beverly and Leavenworth into Kansas City. Approximated: about 11 mi of short straight bridges south of Oelwein (Leavenworth - Kansas City 4.2 mi, Savannah - St. Joseph 1.9, Waterloo - Cedar Falls Junction 1.8, Rosendale/Guilford 1.3), plus the 12 mi carried over from the Minneapolis - Oelwein portion. The St. Joseph and Kansas City terminal legs are drawn on today's track layout, which has changed since 1962.

segments.note: Through Twin Cities - Kansas City service over the CGW's own Oelwein - St. Joseph main line. The Chicago, St. Paul & Kansas City built south from Des Moines and reached St. Joseph in 1890 and Kansas City in 1891; the Leavenworth portion was completed under the Chicago Great Western name in 1895. Headway is an estimate for roughly two through trains a day each way in the busier decades - it is not read off a timetable, and service thinned steadily from the 1930s.
sources: Segment-level: the 1890/1891/1895 construction dates are from the sources below; the headway is an unsourced estimate and the 1891 start is the completion of the route, not a documented first passenger timetable.

segments.note: After the Chicago trains quit in August 1956 the CGW was down to two through passenger trains, and this was one of them: the Mill Cities Limited, trains 5 and 6, Minneapolis - St. Paul - Oelwein - Waterloo - Des Moines - Kansas City. Trains 5 and 6 made their final runs on 27 April 1962 (one account puts train 5 at St. Joseph on its last run on 28 April 1962 - the two are probably the same southbound trip crossing midnight, but the conflict is recorded rather than resolved). One train a day each way. Freight continued over most of the route; the CGW itself was merged into the Chicago & North Western on 1 July 1968.
sources: Segment-level: the 27 April 1962 last run of trains 5 and 6 and the 'only two through trains left after 1956' framing are from american-rails' CGW page; chicagorailfan lists trains 5/6 as the Mill Cities Limited, Minneapolis-St. Paul-Oelwein-Waterloo-Des Moines-Kansas City, discontinued 1962. The 28 April variant is noted in Classic Trains' CGW gallery captions.

properties.line: Chicago Great Western: Nebraska Limited (Twin Cities – Omaha)
properties.speed_source: Estimate only: no CGW timetable was consulted. 358 mi overnight in roughly 11 h would be about 33 mph = 52 km/h.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 358 mi Minneapolis - St. Paul - Hayfield - Austin - Lyle - Manly - Mason City - Clarion - Fort Dodge - Council Bluffs - Omaha against about 354 mi derived from the ICC valuation of the Mason City & Fort Dodge (Hayfield - Manly Junction about 49 mi, Manly Junction - Mason City 9.20, Mason City - Fort Dodge 72.60, Fort Dodge - Council Bluffs 132.87) plus the traced Hayfield - Minneapolis and about 3 mi over the Missouri into Omaha - 1% long. Mason City - Fort Dodge traced 73.1 mi against 72.60 documented and Fort Dodge - Omaha traced 135.0 mi against 132.87 + about 3 mi documented, so those two legs are essentially exact. Nearly all real geometry: the abandoned CGW grade Hayfield - Brownsdale - Austin - Lyle - Manly, the UP Albert Lea Subdivision into Mason City, the Cerro Gordo County Trail, the CGW Fort Dodge Subdivision Belmond - Clarion - Eagle Grove - Fort Dodge, the CGW abandoned grade and Roelyn Industrial Lead Fort Dodge - Lake City - Carroll - Manning - Harlan - Minden, and the Iowa Interstate into Council Bluffs. Approximated: one 8 mi straight line south-west of Mason City where the Cerro Gordo County Trail is not mapped, 2.3 mi at Swaledale, 2.7 mi at Mantorville Junction and 0.7 mi at Rosemount (both carried over from the Minneapolis - Hayfield portion), 1.0 mi at Ralston and 0.6 mi crossing the Missouri River - about 15 mi of 358 in total. The Council Bluffs - Omaha leg is drawn on today's bridge and terminal layout, which is not the 1904-1965 one.

segments.note: Through Twin Cities - Omaha service. The CGW took over the Mason City & Fort Dodge in March 1901, built the Manly Junction - Mason City link in 1901-02 as part of a deliberate plan to reach Omaha, and put the new 132.87 mi Fort Dodge - Council Bluffs line into operation on 1 January 1904, with trackage rights over the Union Pacific's Missouri River bridge into Omaha. Trains over this route carried names including the Nebraska Limited, Omaha Express, Omaha Limited, Twin Cities Express and Twin City Limited. Headway is an estimate for roughly two trains a day each way - it is not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the March 1901 takeover, the 1901-02 Manly Junction link, the 132.91/132.87 mi Fort Dodge - Council Bluffs line and its 1 January 1904 opening, and the UP bridge trackage rights are from the ICC valuation summary of the Mason City & Fort Dodge; the train names from american-rails. The headway is an unsourced estimate.

segments.note: The last CGW passenger service of all: the overnight Twin Cities - Omaha pair, trains 13 and 14, advertised as the Nebraska Limited and the Twin City Limited. The final southbound left Omaha's Burlington Station on 29 September 1965 and the two trains reached their respective endpoints on 30 September 1965, after which the CGW carried no passengers at all for its last two and a half years - it was merged into the Chicago & North Western on 1 July 1968. One train a day each way.
sources: Segment-level: the 30 September 1965 end of passenger operations is from the Wikipedia CGW article; american-rails puts the final departure from Omaha's Burlington Station on 29 September 1965. chicagorailfan lists trains 13/14 Nebraska Limited / Twin City Limited, Minneapolis-St. Paul-Omaha, discontinued 1965.

properties.speed_source: Estimate only. A McKeen-car local over 97 mi of secondary main line; about 28 mph = 45 km/h is a guess, not a timetable figure.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 97.1 mi Oelwein - Waverly - Hampton - Clarion against about 96 mi documented in the ICC valuation of the Mason City & Fort Dodge (Oelwein - Waverly 29.25 mi built 1904, Waverly - Hampton about 40 mi among the 89.38 mi of segments purchased in 1905, Clarion - Hampton 26.83 mi built 1902) - 1% long. Almost all real geometry: the abandoned CGW grade Oelwein - Oran - Readlyn, the Waverly Rail Trail, the Rolling Prairie Trail Shell Rock - Clarksville - Allison - Bristow - Dumont, and the CGW abandoned grade Hampton - Coulter - Rowan - Clarion. One straight-line substitution, 12 mi between Hansell and Hampton where nothing of the grade is in OSM. The split of the 89.38 mi 'purchased 1905' figure between Hayfield - Manly Junction and Waverly - Hampton is my own inference from the geography, not a documented breakdown.

segments.note: The eastern arm of the CGW's Omaha line, joining the Chicago - Twin Cities main at Oelwein to the Mason City - Fort Dodge line at Clarion, and the route by which through Chicago - Omaha trains left the main line. Clarion - Hampton was built in 1902 and Oelwein - Waverly in 1904, with the Waverly - Hampton link among the lines the Mason City & Fort Dodge purchased in 1905, so the through route dates from about 1905; the exact year the first through passenger train ran over it is not established here. By 1950 it was down to a local: McKeen motor car 1003 worked train 35, Oelwein - Clarion, and made No. 35's last run at Oelwein on 26 June 1950, with the connecting Clarion - Omaha train 31 running to Omaha the same month. Drawn to 1950 for that reason - freight went on for decades afterwards and much of the grade is now the Rolling Prairie and Waverly rail trails. One train a day each way.
sources: Segment-level: the 1902/1904/1905 construction and purchase dates are from the ICC valuation summary of the Mason City & Fort Dodge. The 26 June 1950 last run of train 35 (Oelwein-Clarion, McKeen car 1003) and the June 1950 Clarion-Omaha train 31 come from the caption text of Classic Trains' Chicago Great Western image gallery, reached through search - the page itself returns 403 and was not read directly, so treat the date as single-sourced.
